title: Core of the Truehearted 2
content:
The restless murmur in the Demon-Subduing Cave finally sputtered out, leaving a thick, uneasy quiet in its wake. Lan Wangji glanced sideways at Wei Wuxian. "Go on."

Su She looked ready to spit fire, but his lips remained glued shut, his throat parched and burning like dry tinder. Yet having his mouth zipped before he could tear into Wei Wuxian wasn't even the worst part—what truly made his blood boil was the sheer, suffocating humiliation of being pinned under Lan Wangji’s thumb. He clawed repeatedly at his own neck in a desperate bid to unpick the silencing spell, but the magic wouldn't budge. Left with no choice, he turned a pleading gaze toward Lan Qiren.

Lan Qiren didn't even blink. Expression carved from frost, he stared straight ahead, refusing to spare the man a single glance. As a clan elder, he could have effortlessly unraveled the charm; and out of filial respect, Lan Wangji wouldn't dare slap the spell back on someone his uncle had just pardoned. But the bad blood between Gusu Lan and Moling Su ran deep, and Lan Qiren was in no mood to play savior.

The message landed loud and clear with the rest of the room: try picking a fight with Wei Wuxian, and Lan Wangji would shut you up on the spot. A wave of cautious silence swept the cavern. Still, there was always that one brave idiot itching to court death.

"Well, well, aren't you living up to the fearsome Yiling Patriarch name?" a cultivator scoffed. "Throwing your weight around like this—planning to gag every single person in the room?"

Wei Wuxian tilted his head. "Odd, isn't it?"

Lan Sizhui blinked. "What is, Senior Wei?"

"Sect Leader Su over there has been acting weird this whole time," Wei Wuxian drawled. "Back when the corpse horde swarmed us outside, he was basically telling everyone who lost their spiritual energy to roll over and die instead of fighting for survival. Now, he's busy cutting off my interrogation. Not to mention he keeps trying to bait me into a temper, almost like he's terrified you lot might live another minute. What kind of logic is that? Is that how allies are supposed to act?"

A few heads began to turn. Come to think of it, Sect Leader Su really had been running his mouth an awful lot today. But without the heavyweights taking the lead, no one wanted to stick their necks out, opting instead for a discreet, watchful silence. Others quietly racked their brains, trying to retrace their steps on the trek up the mountain.

Wei Wuxian’s eyes drifted toward the Moling Su contingent. They stood conspicuously far from the Gusu Lan disciples, and the latter didn't even deign to look in their direction. The lingering bad blood was palpable.

Leaning toward Lan Wangji, Wei Wuxian lowered his voice: "Hanguang-jun, indulge me for a second. Gusu Lan and Moling Su are both musical sects, and your territories border each other down in Jiangnan. Usually, neighbors get along reasonably well. Why does it feel like your clans despise each other?"

Hearing the question, Lan Sizhui and Lan Jingyi immediately squeezed their way over. Lan Jingyi blurted out, "Of course we despise them!"

Lan Wangji murmured, "Moling Su is an offshoot that splintered from Gusu Lan."

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "Say what?"

Lan Sizhui clamped a hand over Lan Jingyi’s mouth, whispering hurriedly, "You wouldn't know, Senior Wei, but Moling Su was founded by an outside-clan disciple who defected from Gusu Lan. Because he couldn't step out from the shadow of the main house, their clan's techniques are practically a copy-paste of ours. They specialize in music cultivation, and even Sect Leader Su Minshan's spiritual weapon is a seven-stringed guqin modeled directly after Hanguang-jun's."

Wei Wuxian glanced back at Su She’s brooding face, thoroughly speechless.

Lan Jingyi pried Sizhui’s fingers off his mouth, huffing indignantly: "That's not even the wildest part! This Sect Leader Su—alright, fine, I'll keep it down!—this guy copies every single move we make, yet throws a massive tantrum if anyone dares suggest he's imitating our Hanguang-jun. He flies off the handle instantly! How does someone that shameless even exist?"

Lan Sizhui hissed an exasperated, "Jingyi!" as the boy's voice climbed.

Too late. Su She had caught every single syllable. His face flushed an ugly, bruised purple, eyes practically spitting sparks. Coughing up a mouthful of blood, he forcefully shattered the silencing spell through raw willpower, though his voice came out sounding like gravel scraped across stone, raspy as a dying old man.

"Ah, the righteous Gusu Lan Clan! Paragons of virtue, the pinnacle of the cultivation world! So this is how you school your disciples!"

Sect Leader Ouyang chimed in nervously, "Sect Leader Su, we have an army of the dead at the gates. Let's not turn on each other now."

"Turn on each other?" Su She sneered. "Take a good look at Gusu Lan! Crawling into bed with Wei Wuxian—since when were they 'our people'?"

That crossed a line. Lan Qiren cast a frosty glare his way without deigning to speak, but a senior guest elder from the Lan Clan bristled with indignation: "Su Minshan, even if you are no longer bound by the Gusu Lan name, you would do well to mind your tongue!"

A Moling Su disciple stepped forward defensively. "Our Sect Leader severed ties with Gusu Lan ages ago! What right do you have to lecture him?"

Lan Jingyi, having sat on a mountain of grievances for far too long, fired straight back: "Your Sect Leader wouldn't have his current stature if Gusu hadn't cultivated him in the first place! Now that he's turning around to bite the hand that fed him, we aren't even allowed to call him out?"

The cavern dissolved into an angry shouting match. Someone from the Moling Su camp barked, "Gusu Lan has thousands of disciples—are you claiming every single one has what it takes to build a sect from the ground up? The arrogance!"

A Lan disciple volleyed right back, "Arrogance? Look who's talking! I wonder which sect's warding melodies are so riddled with mistakes they don't even realize they're butchering the score!"

The insult hit Wei Wuxian like a flash of lightning.

The pieces snapped together in his mind.

"It wasn't the food, and it wasn't the regional feng shui!" he blurted out.

The cavern went quiet. Wei Wuxian swept his gaze across the crowd. "You're all missing the obvious. There is one specific thing every single one of you did after marching onto this mountain."

Lan Sizhui asked, "What was it?"

"Fighting off the walking corpses."

Ouyang Zizhen gasped, putting two and two together. "Wait, like what happened back in Yi City? Was there corpse-poison powder packed into their bodies? Dad, when you were hacking through that horde, did any strange powder burst out of them?"

Sect Leader Ouyang shook his head flatly. "No powder, none at all!"

Zizhen pressed, "What about... a weird fluid?"

Jiang Cheng’s patience snapped. "Enough. If some foul mist or poison had sprayed out when we cut them down, we wouldn't all be oblivious to it."

Realizing he’d run down a blind alley, Zizhen flushed crimson and scratched the back of his neck, while his father hastily hauled the excitable kid back into his seat.

Wei Wuxian continued, "It is tied to cutting down the dead. But the trap wasn't woven into the corpses—it came from the people fighting them."

Turning his attention toward Lan Qiren, he offered an easy smile. "Senior Lan, mind if I ask you a question?"

Lan Qiren cut a sideways glance toward Lan Wangji, responding with stone-cold indifference: "Whatever questions you have, can't you ask him instead of bothering me?"

Lan Qiren was an unbending traditionalist, but he was no fool. He had long smelled something rotten in the air, which was the only reason he’d sat through the interrogation this long without flipping a table. His scowl was dark as a thundercloud, but Wei Wuxian had spent his entire youth getting glared at by this man—and his entire adulthood getting glared at by the rest of the world—so it rolled right off him like water off a duck's back. Rubbing his chin, he chuckled, "I was just worried that grilling him right in front of your face would get on your nerves. But since you gave me the green light... Lan Zhan?"

Lan Wangji answered steadily, "Mm."

"Moling Su splintered off from Gusu Lan, right?"

"Mm."

"And despite breaking away, their signature techniques were heavily 'borrowed' from Gusu Lan, correct?"

"Yes."

"One of Gusu Lan's secret arts is the Cleansing Chords, used to banish malevolence and repel dark spirits," Wei Wuxian laid out smoothly. "The seven-stringed guqin is the most intricate and profound vehicle for this discipline, which is why most of your disciples specialize in it. Moling Su played copycat, so the vast majority of their cultivators are zither players too, right?"

"Correct."

"And even though Sect Leader Su poached those arts to set up his own house, his personal mastery of the instrument isn't exactly groundbreaking, and his disciples often bumble through their melodies with clumsy, glaring mistakes—isn't that so?"

Lan Wangji didn't sugarcoat it. "It is."

Back and forth, the two volleyed questions and answers as if nobody else existed in the room. Slowly but surely, the crowd realized this wasn't just petty mockery aimed at Su She; Wei Wuxian was peeling back the layers of a trap, and they leaned in, hanging on every word.

Wei Wuxian’s tone dropped into a measured, chilling cadence.

"...Which means, even if an off-key, jarring melody slipped into the battle chords played by the Moling Su Clan during the ascent, Gusu Lan wouldn't think twice about it. They would just roll their eyes, chalking it up to sloppy technique and bad memorization, never stopping to wonder whether the flawed notes were an honest mistake... or entirely deliberate. Am I warm?"

Su She’s pupils shrunk to pinpricks. Veins bulged violently along the back of his hand, and his sword cleared its scabbard by a fraction of an inch. At the exact same moment, Lan Wangji lifted his gaze, meeting Wei Wuxian's eyes with mutual, unspoken clarity.

"Precisely," Lan Wangji affirmed, cutting through the silence.

A sharp metallic hiss rang out as Su She drew his blade. Wei Wuxian casually flicked the edge aside with two fingers, his smirk dripping with easy confidence. "What's the steel for? Don't forget, your spiritual power is completely shot. You think threatening me with dead iron is going to work?"

Hovering between a lunge and a retreat, Su She gritted his teeth, snarling, "You've been circling around me this whole time—what filthy insinuations are you trying to spin?!"

"Did I speak too softly for you?" Wei Wuxian countered. "Fine, let me spell it out so even the cheap seats can hear. Everyone here lost their spiritual energy because you all did the exact same thing: you fought walking corpses. And while you were hacking through them, Sect Leader Su of Moling Su was marching right beside you. He pretended to play warding chords to repel the dead, but quietly spliced a foreign melody into the score—a cursed tune designed to drain a cultivator's golden core. You thought he had your back in the trenches, but he was quietly stabbing you in the spine..."

"Slander!" Su She spat.

Wei Wuxian ignored him, turning to the crowd. "There are plenty of Gusu Lan zither players in this cave, aren't there? Tell me: on the way up the mountain, were there mistakes in the scores played by Moling Su?"

As the undisputed masters of the craft, the Lan cultivators answered in absolute, ringing unison: "There were!"

"Sect Leader Su knew full well that Gusu Lan looked down on him, and he weaponized that disdain," Wei Wuxian laid bare. "Cursed music requires immense spiritual reserves to take effect. Pulling off an incantation capable of crippling a thousand cultivators was far beyond what he could manage alone, so he brought along every single zither player in his clan to harmonize with him! Gusu Lan was the only house capable of catching the discrepancy, but they couldn't be bothered to pay him any mind. Even if they heard a wrong note, they simply assumed he was a second-rate hack who taught his students poorly!"

Nie Huaisang gaped, eyes wide. "There’s actually a cursed tune out there that can strip a man's spiritual power just by listening to it?!"

"Why wouldn't there be?" Wei Wuxian replied. "If music can banish demons, why couldn't it summon malice? There is an esoteric scorebook from the Eastern Seas known as the Collection of Turmoil, detailing forbidden, lethal songs—some capable of taking a life on the spot. Why would a melody that temporarily neutralizes a golden core be out of the question? Senior Lan Qiren is standing right here. Ask him yourself: does such a manuscript exist within the forbidden archives beneath the Library Pavilion of Gusu Lan?"

Forcing down the panic crawling up his spine, Su She let out a strained sneer. "Even if such a piece exists, back when I studied in Gusu, I didn't have the clearance to step foot into the forbidden archives! I haven't set foot in the Cloud Recesses since my departure, and I've never heard of this so-called Collection of Turmoil! If anything, you seem suspiciously familiar with it. And given your cozy little relationship with Hanguang-jun, aren't you far more likely to have had access to it than I ever did?"

Wei Wuxian chuckled softly. "Who said you had to sneak into the forbidden archives yourself? Your master comes and goes as he pleases, doesn't he? I'd wager he was the one who handed you the altered score in the first place."

A high-ranking figure who enjoyed unrestricted access to the Cloud Recesses, pulling Su She’s strings from the shadows—there was only one name that fit the bill.

Lianfang-zun!

"It was a brilliant setup," Wei Wuxian continued, unspooling the thread. "Kidnap the clan heirs, draw an army of cultivators up to the Burial Mounds, and set the board. He feigned an injury back at Koi Tower to dodge suspicion, leaving you to handle the inside job. You crippled everyone's spiritual cores with the cursed song, while he used the Yin Tiger Tally to herd a legion of fierce corpses to trap you all on the mountain. When a thousand prominent cultivators get butchered on my doorstep, who else would the world blame?

"Even running into me didn't derail your plans. My reputation is in the gutter anyway; with old grudges boiling over, nobody was going to listen to my defense. If you pushed me hard enough, maybe I'd snap and paint the mountain in blood myself, saving you the trouble of dirtying your own hands."

Su She scoffed loudly, "Absurd! Lianfang-zun is already the Chief Cultivator, sitting at the pinnacle of the prominent clans! He has no rivals to conquer—what possible benefit would he gain from sending hundreds of lives to the slaughter? Dragging my name through the mud is one thing, but you dare sling slander at Lianfang-zun?!"

Wei Wuxian’s eyes narrowed into a razor-thin smile. "Since you're so thoroughly convinced of your innocence, how about a demonstration? Why don't you play the exact warding piece your clan used on the way up the mountain, right here in front of everyone?"

Every master of the zither from Gusu Lan was standing in the cavern. If Su She changed a single note from his earlier performance, they would catch him in a heartbeat!

The surrounding crowd quietly shuffled backward, putting as much distance between themselves and Moling Su as possible, leaving them stranded in a glaring island of empty space.

Wei Wuxian pressed his advantage. "Reluctant? Fine by me. Why don't you take a look at this instead?"

Reaching into his inner lapel, he pulled out two yellowed sheets of parchment, waving them casually just enough for the ink strokes of musical notation to be visible. "Did you honestly think we came away empty-handed from Koi Tower? Behind the bronze mirror in the Fragrance Palace, Jin Guangyao had two torn pages from the Collection of Turmoil tucked away in his hidden vault. We found them. All it takes is handing these to Senior Lan Qiren to see if the melody matches what you played outside, and the truth comes out."

Su She’s jaw tightened into a rigid sneer. "Liar. How do I know you didn't just scribble some gibberish onto scrap paper to frame me?"

"Do I look like the type of guy who casually carries spare sheet music in his robes?" Wei Wuxian countered. "Whether I'm bluffing or not, Senior Lan will know the second he lays eyes on it."

Su She had suspected a bluff, but the chilling certainty in Wei Wuxian's smirk and the deepening scowl on Lan Qiren’s brow made cold dread flood his veins. Panic seized him.

"Senior Lan, it's a trick!" he blurted out, lunging forward with an outstretched hand to snatch the papers.

A streak of azure sword-glare whistled through the air. Bichen struck!

Su She drew his spiritual blade on pure instinct, meeting the strike head-on. But the instant the metals collided, a sickening realization hit him like a physical blow:

He'd taken the bait.

His blade, named Nanping—meaning "Never at Peace"—glowed with a brilliant, crackling aura as it parried Bichen.

A spiritual glare radiating with undiluted, peak golden core power.
